content_html:
Raccoons return to trash cans when they find an easy food source, so lasting prevention combines a lid they cannot open, fewer accessible food odors, and placement that does not make the container easy to tip or climb. There is no need to approach or corner the animal.

Use a lid that actually locks

A loose lid or light hinge can be lifted with paws. Use built-in latches, straps, or a wildlife-resistant enclosure, while making sure the setup still works with normal trash collection.

Reduce food odors and rewards

Drain food containers, close bags that contain scraps, and clean spills from the lid and sides. Where local rules allow it, keep especially smelly waste in a closed area until collection day rather than leaving it outside for several days.

Make the can harder to tip or reach

Place the container on a stable surface and away from fences, trees, or furniture that provide leverage. A small ventilated, sturdy enclosure can be more effective than simply adding weight inside the can.

If a raccoon appears, give it space and an exit

Do not corner, feed, or handle it. Keep people and pets inside, remove the attractant after the animal leaves, and contact wildlife control if it is injured, trapped, or behaving abnormally.
